top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Edinburgh
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Edinburgh Potential Reserves (mmboe): P99 1.5, P90 4.9, P50 68.7, P10 595.0, P1 1779.6, Mean 211.5 (Mean = P28); lognormal plot
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Pre-Chalk prospect straddling the Norway/UK border at the SE end of the Josephine Ridge: candidate Upper Jurassic Fulmar/Freshney and Triassic Skagerrak sandstones below the BCU, trapped by dip closure to the S and E and by faults (towards the dry 30/13-7 well) and salt walls to the N and W. Mandal Fm source mature for oil, most likely fluid gas condensate; Pg 44 %, mean potential reserves 211.5 MMboe for the whole structure. Considered drillable by all partners, but only ~19-22 % lies in PL660 and the four-licence joint well agreement could not be signed for commercial reasons.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Kelvin
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Recoverable gas BCM Kelvin: P90 10.8, P50 24.2, P10 55.9, Mean 29.4
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Cretaceous Nise gas prospect NE of Celsius, defined through the licence work on the new 3D; only partly in PL653 and mainly in open acreage (block 6608/1, recommended for an APA 2014 application). Recoverable gas P50 24.2 GSm3 (mean 29.4), Pg 35 % after DHI uplift; of interest for a potential area development.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Sjampis
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Table 3 Sjampis Stø: Oil case, recoverable MSm3 P90/Mean/P10 = 6.0 35.5 78.0
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Main prospect: shallow marine shoreface sandstones of the Lower-Middle Jurassic Stø Formation in a small 3-way faulted dip closure in a downfaulted, rotated fault block, with potential deeper sealing against the Finnmark Platform boundary fault, about 5 km from the 7019/1-1 Gamma gas discovery. Charge by spill from Gamma (Hekkingen source) with oil expected; stacked secondary segments in Knurr, Snadd and Kobbe. Pg 0.25, mean 35.5 MSm3 oil (oil case); no DHI and the main risk is trap seal along a fault that breaches the sea floor.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Fjellflokk Far East 1
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Recoverable gas [10^9 Sm3] P90 8,60 / Mode 12,80 / Mean 13,90 / P10 19,70 (text p.23: mean recoverable volume of 491 bcf gas; Table 4.2: 491 bcf / 13.9 bcm)
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Nise 1 turbidite sandstone (Nise Fm, Campanian per Table 4.3) in a faulted 4-way dip closure formed by E-W inversion of a N-S normal fault on the Naglefar Dome in block 6707/4 (PL847B); gas with good amplitude conformance to structure (switch-off ~3200 m TVDSS, 14 km2). Mean recoverable 491 bcf (13.90 GSm3) gas, COS 60 % - trap effectiveness (gas leakage along faults) the only risk. Remaining prospectivity of significance, but not economically viable at relinquishment.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Bjørk Intra Heather Lower
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Lower level of the Bjørk Intra Heather (Upper Jurassic, Callovian-Early Oxfordian, Heather-Fensfjord) oil prospect south of the J2 discovery and directly west of the Øygarden Fault Complex, bound by faults to the north and south and dip to the west and east, charged by long-distance migration or remigration from Draupne/Heather source. It was the primary prospect at licence award, mapped on a strong amplitude anomaly, and was dropped when AVO and fluid substitution showed the anomaly was probably coal.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Svartbakkestjerne Springar
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: total of 663bcf recoverable gas - the sum of mean values for all three conformable reservoir units (Table 4.2: 663 bcf / 18.8 bcm)
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Series of stacked thin sands (Springar 1, 2 and 4) in the uppermost Springar Fm (Maastrichtian) on the Svartbakkestjerne structure, seen as high-amplitude anomalies with overall conformance to structure (10-15 km2) in a 3-way closure against a major E-W fault that may have been protected from late gas leakage. Gas; 663 bcf total mean recoverable (sum of three units), COS 42 % per unit with trap effectiveness (0.6) and reservoir presence (0.7) risks. Not economically viable at relinquishment.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Jaktfalk
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Table 3 Jaktfalk, Tubåen: P90 Oil (10^6 Sm3) 10.7, P50 Oil 23.3, P10 Oil 48.7, Pmean Oil 27.1 (basis/risking not labelled; recoverable assumed as Table 2)
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Tilted fault block/horst trap in the transition zone between the Hammerfest and Nordkapp basins with the main target in the Stø-Tubåen (Tubåen) Formation and secondary Fruholmen and Snadd targets (segment records). APA 2010: base 9.68 MSm3 oil, Pg 0.22. New 3D and inversion showed the Tubåen thins to 0-20 m (near or below seismic resolution) over Jaktfalk, which significantly reduced the volumes; closure in the east not certain. Dropped for reservoir presence and retention risk and small volumes.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Faering East (Ula)
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Upper Jurassic Ula Fm shoreface prospect on the tilted Triassic pod east of Faering South, outside PL809; trap defined by pinch-out of the Ula shoreface and/or erosional truncation at BCU to the east and north-east. MUR 136 Mboe, POS 34 %; critical risk structural geometry. No Ula-level prospectivity inside PL809.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Maiblom
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Largest prospect in PL944: combined structural-stratigraphic pinch-out trap of the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian) Springar Fm deep-marine sandstones, down dip of the Gro gas discovery, with patchy class 3 AVO / low-impedance support. Gas expected; 162 km2, mean 143 mmboe recoverable, POSg 32 %. Dropped: significant risk of residual gas in poor-quality (around 1 mD) reservoir and negative economics.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Faering South
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Sand 2: MUR 146Mboe with POS 29% (Fig. 1: "Sand-2: 146 Mboe; PG:29%"; p.7 "prospective resources (aggregate UMR) of 146Mboe")
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Upper Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Farsund Fm turbidite sands (Sand-1 and Sand-2) deposited in the Faering mini-graben, embedded in the Farsund source rock. Strati-structural combined trap: turbidites disconnected from the up-dip shoreface to the east by pinch-out and fault compartmentalization, with south and west facies terminations from RMS amplitude maps. HP/HT gas-condensate prospect (Sand-1 MUR 92 Mboe POS 24 %, Sand-2 MUR 146 Mboe POS 29 %); critical risk lateral seal; King Lear Farsund turbidite discovery is the main analogue.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Firebird
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Firebird, Brent Group: P90 21.4, P50 72.8, Mean 122.3, P10 275.5 (mm stb oe), Table 4.1 image
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Middle Jurassic Ness and Tarbert (Brent Gp) shallow marine sandstones, with a secondary Statfjord Fm target, in a large low-relief three-way dip closure against the hangingwall of the SE-NW fault system bounding the Utsira High (faulted hangingwall block at Top Brent, top reservoir ~2750-2770 m MSL). Charge from Draupne/Heather shales of a mature westerly Viking Graben kitchen; oil expected. Mean 122.3 MMboe recoverable, GPOS 28 %, but fault seal/trap integrity is a critical risk that cannot be reduced.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Sweetums South Norian
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Sweetums South Norian: segment of the Sweetums Prospect in Norian marginal-marine to estuarine Snadd Fm sand on the lower flank of the eastern salt diapir, defined by semi-conformant AVO and low-velocity anomalies. Segments split on a ~30 m difference in DFI shut-off; up-dip stratigraphic seal needed and trap risk high (P2 0.25), Pg 0.22.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Fannaråken
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Large HPHT Upper Jurassic Ula/Gyda prospect on the eastern flank of the Breiflabb Basin, a west-east three-way dip closure sealed by faults, salt walls and pinch-out, seen as an extension of the Peking Duck trend and likely already tested by the Peking Duck Discovery wells 7/11-12S and A. Mean 11.86 MSm3 oil + 14.40 GSm3 gas, COS 30 %; medium to high risk, would need an additional HPHT well. Not drilled; licence relinquished.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Arenaria
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Recoverable Non Assoc. Gas [1e9 Sm3], success volume MC(5000): Mode 6.94, Mean 7.61, Std.dev 1.83, P100 3.92, P90 5.44, P50 7.39, P10 10.1, P0 13.3 (text p.12: "mean recoverable volumes of 7.1 GSm3 gas")
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Middle Triassic (Anisian) Kobbe Fm sandstones deposited in a tidal/coastal-plain setting with tidal channels, on the Bjarmeland Platform; gas proven in tight Kobbe reservoir at four levels by 7224/6-1 (drilled 2008 outside the seismically visible channels). Applied for as a 3-way dip closure (493 km2, Pg 32 %, base 52.9 GSm3 gas) on the idea that wells in the channels would find better reservoir; after Norvarg-2 and Langlitinden found poor, clay-rich channel sands it was heavily downgraded to a 95 km2 stratigraphic channel trap (Pg 0.56, mean recoverable gas 7.1-7.6 GSm3), judged very limited and not economical.

top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.name: Birkeland
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.original_text: Recoverable gas BCM Birkeland: P90 5.2, P50 11, P10 19.6, Mean 10.6
top_15_apa_open_for_manual_audit.conclusion_summary: Upper Cretaceous Nise (Tumler/Spekkhogger) turbidite sandstone gas prospect on Utgard High South in PL694 (west of Eyde, around well 6607/5-1); APA 2012 prospect, still a prospect after mapping of the new broadband 3D, with resources reduced from 6,90 to P50 11 GSm3 (mean 10.6) and Pg 46 % -> 39 % after DHI uplift. Originally a strongly amplitude-driven combined structural/stratigraphic trap; amplitudes on the new data are more restricted to structural closures.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Lower level of the Bjørk Intra Heather (Upper Jurassic, Callovian-Early Oxfordian, Heather-Fensfjord) oil prospect south of the J2 discovery and directly west of the Øygarden Fault Complex, bound by faults to the north and south and dip to the west and east, charged by long-distance migration or remigration from Draupne/Heather source. It was the primary prospect at licence award, mapped on a strong amplitude anomaly, and was dropped when AVO and fluid substitution showed the anomaly was probably coal.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Upper Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) Farsund Fm turbidite sands (Sand-1 and Sand-2) deposited in the Faering mini-graben, embedded in the Farsund source rock. top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Fannaråken
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Large HPHT Upper Jurassic Ula/Gyda prospect on the eastern flank of the Breiflabb Basin, a west-east three-way dip closure sealed by faults, salt walls and pinch-out, seen as an extension of the Peking Duck trend and likely already tested by the Peking Duck Discovery wells 7/11-12S and A. top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Irpa
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.original_text: Fig. 4.5 Irpa recoverable volume range, accumulation size Total Resources [1e6 STB OE]: P99 1.49, P90 4.44, P68 9.41, P50 27.7, Mean 77.4, P10 249.4, P1 450.8; P10/P90 = 56
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Lower-Middle Jurassic Brent Gp (Tarbert, Ness, Etive, Oseberg) to top Cook Fm sandstones in five stacked intervals at >4100 m on the Flatfisk Slope, Block 30/3. Structural trap: 3-way dip closure against the Veslefrikk bounding fault plus a larger down-dip closure that depends on the low-offset Flank Fault sealing; charged from Draupne/Heather mainly from the Magne sub-basin, gas-condensate expected. Main driver of the APA 2017 application; COS 29 % (58 % for the 3-way part), recoverable mean 11.30 GSm3 gas + 1.70 MSm3 liquids; not economic - negative drill decision Q1 2020.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Karius
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.original_text: Recoverable Gas [10^9 Sm3]: Low (P90) 3.70, Base Mode 6.10, Base Mean 11.20, High (P10) 22.10 (Table 4.1: 3.7-11.2-22.10)
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Main prospect of PL763: Santonian-Campanian Nise Fm basin-floor-fan sandstones in a 3-way dip, fault dependent closure against a SW-NE trending normal fault on the southern flange of the Vema Dome, about 20 km SW of the Aasta Hansteen discoveries. Charge from the Nagrid Syncline (Lange and Spekk Fm source rocks); dry gas with small amounts of condensate expected, mean recoverable 11.20 GSm3 gas, Pg 25.8 %. Main risk lateral (fault) seal from possible thief sands in the footwall, plus migration (no clear DHI). Recommended for drilling by the operator but not supported by the partners; relinquished.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Lienz
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.original_text: Recoverable resources, Gas [10^9 Sm3], main phase: 3.03 / 9.46 (mode) / 11.10 (mean) / 20.80; Table 4.1 PL1004 Update 2021: 3.03 / 11.10 / 20.80
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Lower Jurassic Åre Formation and Upper Triassic Grey Beds fluvio-deltaic sands in the Høgbraken Horst, a fault-bounded horst below the dry Frusalen well 6507/11-10 on the eastern Halten Terrace, sealed by uppermost Åre Fm shale and large-offset boundary faults. Charge by migration from the Gimsan Basin kitchen and spill from Yttergryta/Midgard; gas with condensate, mean 11.10 GSm3 gas + 0.55 MSm3 liquid recoverable, Pd 0.26 (2021; APA 2018 0.24). Not drilled: licence surrendered when the partners could not agree on a DoD extension.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Serendipity
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Upper Jurassic sub-unconformity stratigraphic trap in Oxfordian Intra-Melke Fm turbidite sandstones encased in Melke shales, in the Gimsan Basin 7 km north-east of Njord. Pg 31 % and mean 8.9 MSm3 oil (65 MMboe) recoverable, economic as a Njord tie-back, but seal (thief sands) and reservoir risk kept the partners from a drill decision.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Rødsildre Nise
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Rødsildre Nise: fault-bounded three-way Nise closure (third from north of four), mean 13.2 million Sm3 oe recoverable, POSg 0.20; higher trap-effectiveness risk in the N-S trend and no amplitude support.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Manilow
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.original_text: Recoverable gas [10^9 Sm3] main phase: Low (P90) 2.09, Base mode 2.98, Base mean 9.47, High (P10) 19.85
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Elongate Jurassic fault block in the Revfallet Fault Complex (boundary Halten Terrace / Nordland Ridge), bounded east and west by normal faults downthrown to the east; Garn Fm primary target with Ile, Tofte and Tilje in the high case; gas/condensate. Final evaluation: recoverable gas mean 9.47 GSm3 (P90 2.09, P10 19.85), Pg 0.24. Key risk reservoir presence (Not vs Åre coal interpretation, possible BCU erosion of Garn-Tofte), plus eastern fault closure and migration; dropped for relatively high risk, modest volumes and unattractive economics.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Mosterøy
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.original_text: Recoverable oil [10^6 Sm3] main phase P90/mode/mean/P10
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Upper Jurassic Intra Draupne Formation deepwater turbidite sandstones (Oxfordian-Ryazanian) on the Gudrun Terrace, sourced from the northern Utsira High along a north-northeast fairway (as for the Gudrun Field). Combined structural/stratigraphic trap sealed by the main bounding north-south fault; Draupne Formation charge at the start of the oil window, oil with a possible gas cap. Pg rose from 0.22 (APA 2014) to 0.32 after fault-seal work; mean recoverable 6.91 MSm3 oil + 1.53 GSm3 gas, positive NPV as a tie-back to Ivar Aasen, but partners disagreed on fault seal and the licence was relinquished undrilled.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Jesper
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.original_text: Table 4.1 P90-Pmean-P10 Recoverable volumes (10^9 Sm3) Gas/Cond: 4.87-8.98-14.41/0.06-0.15-0.27
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Nise Fm (Santonian-Campanian) prospect in PL763, one of five Nise prospects identified on ST10004 3D and shown on Figure 4.1; gas and condensate expected, recoverable gas P90-Pmean-P10 4.87-8.98-14.41 GSm3, geological chance of success 0.23. Only listed in Table 4.1 and on the map - no separate description; Karius was preferred as the main prospect and the licence was relinquished.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Hakone Tithonian Upper
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Intra-Draupne Tithonian forced-regression delta-front sandstone in an Oxfordian unconformity canyon off the Amoco High, trapped by up-dip BCU truncation and down-dip shale-out. Mean 5.67 MSm3 o.e. (35.7 MMboe) recoverable with CoS 0.38; reservoir quality is the main risk. A Snorre A tie-back was uneconomic (MEFS 25 MMboe; P50 only marginal).

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: AiSuma
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Middle Jurassic Ile Formation structural prospect in the south of PL1113, 7 km from Draugen; the APA 2020 Thule lead (Ile/Tofte Fms, 3-way closure) matured by OKEA into a drill-ready prospect. Pg 0.30 with trap/fault seal the main risk and charge by oil spill from Tau supported by shows; mean 5.95 MSm3 (37.4 MMbbl) recoverable oil. Not drilled only because no drilling partner was found before the DoD deadline.

top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.name: Sokna
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.original_text: Reserves Total MMBOE: P90 1.57, P50 13.35, P10 63, MSV 25 (gas and condensate; mean technical recoverable 25 MMboe, p. 3)
top_15_tieback_le30km_apa_open.conclusion_summary: Stacked Jurassic Garn, Ile (Mid Jurassic) and Tofte, Tilje (Lower Jurassic) sandstones preserved below the BCU in two graben pockets (Sokna 1 and 2) west of Erlend, in a down-faulted dip-closure that depends completely on up-dip fault seal. Charged locally from Spekk, Melke and Are source rocks in the gas-condensate window; expected gas and condensate. Mean recoverable 25 MMboe with GPOS 43 % (at least one level) at ~5100 m in an HPHT setting - too risky, small and costly to drill.
